headline: In month 9 you’ll want to know what month 2 looked like.
sub: Your memory won’t keep it. Your log will.
caption:
TSW moves slowly. When you’re sleeping four hours a night, last month blurs into this one.

A daily log in Skinpal takes about 30 seconds: mood, where you’re flaring on the body map, sleep, stress, food and notes. Over the weeks you get a weekly summary and the patterns in your own data. When someone asks “is it better than before?” you can open the app and check.

question: What gets you through a night when the itch won’t stop?
caption:
Let’s talk about sleep.

Nights are where TSW hits hardest for a lot of us. Not because of one thing, but because of all of it at once: itch, heat, chills, waking up stuck to the sheets.

What gets you through those nights? A routine, a playlist, a podcast, a person you text at 3am? Share it below so someone awake tonight can read it.

This is community experience, not medical advice. Talk to your doctor about treatment.

title: Month 58
lines: Progress is hard to see from inside one bad week.
Looking back over months is the only way I can tell what has changed.
caption:
58 months.

I started TSW on 27 January 2022. I’m still healing, and I’m still here posting about it.

What I know now that I didn’t in month 1: progress is hard to see from inside a single bad week. Looking back over months is the only way I can tell what has changed.

Which month are you on? Comment your number. I read them.

#tsw #topicalsteroidwithdrawal #tswjourney #tswwarrior #tswcommunity #eczema

body: Two questions I couldn’t answer in my hardest months. So I built an app that can.
caption:
Two questions I couldn’t answer in the hardest months of TSW:

Is it getting better?
What made today worse?

I didn’t have the data. Nobody I knew did. That’s why we built Skinpal: a simple daily log for mood, symptoms, sleep, stress and food, so you can look back and see what has changed.

It doesn’t treat anything. It helps you keep track.

Free for 14 days. Follow @skinpal.app or find the link in my bio.

headline: Skinpal grew out of a patient community.
caption:
Skinpal grew out of a patient community.

Our founder Lukas has lived with topical steroid withdrawal (TSW) since January 2022 and shares it openly on @tswlukas. That account became a TSW community of 40,000+ followers across platforms, and the questions people asked there shaped the product.

Three things that community taught us about building a health app:

1. People don’t want more information. They want to know if today is better or worse than last month. So the core of Skinpal is a 30-second daily log, not a content library.

2. The community answers faster than any FAQ. Someone is always awake at 3am who has been through the same thing. We build for that instead of around it.

3. Trust comes from lived experience. That shapes every product decision, including what we won’t do: Skinpal doesn’t diagnose or treat.

If you work in dermatology, patient advocacy or digital health, we’d like to hear from you.

#digitalhealth #healthtech #patientcommunity #eczema #startup

headline: Appointments are short. Memory is shorter.
sub: A daily log turns “it’s been bad lately” into something a doctor can work with.
caption:
Appointments are short. Memory is shorter.

People living with chronic skin conditions are often asked a simple question at the doctor’s office: “Has it been better or worse since last time?” After weeks of poor sleep, that is surprisingly hard to answer.

Skinpal gives patients a simple daily log: where they’re flaring on a body map, daily impact, stress, sleep and food. Over time it becomes a weekly summary they can bring to an appointment.

Not a diagnosis. Not a treatment. Just better information in the room.

We’re curious: if you’re a clinician, what would you want a patient to bring?

#dermatology #digitalhealth #patientreportedoutcomes #eczema #healthtech

headline: Building for a condition most people have never heard of.
caption:
We’re TSW Nordic AB, a small Swedish company building Skinpal: a tracking and community app for people with topical steroid withdrawal (TSW) and eczema.

TSW is discussed by large online communities every day, yet many people outside them have never heard the term. Those communities are where Skinpal started, and they are who we build for.

What Skinpal does today:
- Daily symptom, mood and sleep logging
- Body map and photo timeline
- Weekly summaries and personal patterns
- Notes for doctor visits
- Community

Available on iOS and Android in English and Spanish.

We’re open to conversations with clinicians, researchers, patient organisations and partners who work with chronic skin conditions. Send us a message.

#healthtech #digitalhealth #eczema #startup #sweden
